problem: Given that ${\lambda }_{1}=6-\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{2}$ are eigenvalues of a real $2\times 2$ matrix $A$, find $3({\lambda }_{1}+{\lambda }_{2}).$
worked_solution:
Since ${\lambda }_{1}=6-\text{i}$ is a complex eigenvalue of $A,$ the second eigenvalue of $A$ must be the complex conjugate of ${\lambda }_{1}.$
Therefore, 

$$
{\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{1}=6+\text{i}.
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}3({\lambda }_{1}+{\lambda }_{2}) & =3(6-\text{i}+(6+\text{i})) \\  & =3(12) \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$
